evals.name: review-existing-checkout
evals.prompt: Review evals/files/Checkout for design problems before we grow 10x. Recommendations only, don't edit anything.
evals.expected_output: A scan-first review: inventory (MySQL, Redis, Stripe, Celery), findings SD001/SD004 (float money), SD002 (FOR UPDATE), SD003 (modulo worker placement), SD007 (rank by COUNT), a missing idempotency key on POST /v1/checkout, MySQL reported as kept because the README documents it, a 10x estimate from the calculator, and recommendations with IDs, sources and statuses.
expectations: Runs scripts/arch_scan.py (or reports its inventory and findings) before recommending anything.
Flags money stored as float in checkout.py and DOUBLE in the migration (SD001/SD004), citing Vol. 2 ch. 11.
Flags that POST /v1/checkout has no idempotency key and that the FOR UPDATE check does not protect against a retried Stripe call, citing Vol. 2 ch. 7 or ch. 11.
Flags hash(seller_id) % len(workers) as modulo placement (SD003), citing Vol. 1 ch. 5.
Flags the seller rank COUNT(*) query (SD007) and proposes a sorted set, citing Vol. 2 ch. 10.
Reports the MySQL choice as kept because the README documents it as deliberate.
Uses scripts/estimate.py (or shows its table) for the 10x traffic figure instead of prose arithmetic.
Every recommendation has a stable REC-NN ID, a source, a trade-off and a status.
No file under evals/files/Checkout is modified.

evals.name: capacity-plan-real-numbers
evals.prompt: Our photo-sharing API has 2M DAU, each uploads 3 photos a day (avg 2 MB) and views 60. We keep photos 3 years. Peak is 3x. What breaks first when we double, and what do we change?
evals.expected_output: Calculator table (writes ~70/s, reads ~1.4k/s, ~12 TB/day, ~13 PB retained), egress as the first bottleneck, CDN and object storage recommendation with cost note, metadata DB read replicas, stateless API tier, each citing Vol. 1 ch. 1 and ch. 14/15 patterns.
expectations: Produces an estimate table with derivations (or the calculator's output) rather than arithmetic in prose.
Identifies egress bandwidth or storage growth as the first bottleneck with a number.
Recommends a CDN and object storage for photos, citing Vol. 1 ch. 1 (CDN) and ch. 14 or ch. 15.
States the trade-off (CDN cost per GB) instead of only the benefit.
Names what to measure after the change.

evals.name: mock-interviewer
evals.prompt: Be my interviewer. Give me a system design question and don't tell me the answer; push back on my choices.
evals.expected_output: One problem statement, scope answers with concrete numbers when asked, no solution revealed, prompts for estimates and a deep dive, and a graded debrief at the end.
expectations: Poses a single system design problem in one or two sentences.
Does not present the architecture or solution unprompted.
Answers scope questions with concrete numbers (users, QPS, retention) the way the chapters do.
Asks the candidate for back-of-the-envelope estimates.
Offers a debrief structured by the framework's steps and dos/don'ts.
